questions.q: How many personality types does the MBTI method described in the summary produce?
a: Sixteen
Eight
Twelve
Twenty-four
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the four personality areas combine into sixteen distinct types.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the difference between judging and perceiving types?
a: Judgers like order while perceivers prefer flexibility
Judgers trust feelings while perceivers trust logic
Judgers enjoy company while perceivers prefer solitude
Judgers focus on the future while perceivers focus on now
questions.why: Lesson 1 pairs judging with organisation and perceiving with a preference for flexibility.

questions.q: What should you examine to spot careers that might suit you?
a: Where your identity meets your interests
Which jobs pay the most in your area
Which industries are growing fastest
What your family expects you to do
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the crossover of who you are and what interests you reveals possible career paths.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest finishing your job hunt?
a: Interview people already doing the work
Send applications to as many firms as possible
Take a second personality test online
Volunteer in a related field for a month
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends talking to people in the role to hear what they like and dislike about it.

questions.q: What does the summary say about changing career direction?
a: It can happen at any age
It is easiest before you turn thirty
It should wait until retirement
It only works with a new qualification
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that as different parts of your personality develop, a new path can make sense at any age.
